events.title: Sìleas nic Rath taken on as the chronicler's clerk
events.body: Raghnall mac Mhuirich, keeper of the Library, finds the wage out of his own fund for binding and takes on Sìleas nic Rath, a copyist's niece of Àth dhìreach, as clerk to Seanchaidh na Rìoghachd. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh had asked the council for a clerk three times and been refused or ignored each time.

events.title: The slip-box of the word's spellings
events.body: At Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's asking, Sìleas nic Rath begins a box of slips, one to a spelling, of every form the fuel's name takes in the letters that come up the library road: dubhan, dùbhan, dùban, and once, for a fortnight only, An Dubhan with the article and a capital letter.

events.title: The maor of Cathair mhòr's letter marked first
events.body: The first letter marked in Sìleas nic Rath's box is the maor of Cathair mhòr's, which speaks of the fair price of dùban and says nothing of the man who first made it. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh reads it for the clerk as the mark of a name going out of its own word.

events.title: Dubhan-tùsail entered and never used
events.body: Raghnall mac Mhuirich copies Scoiltean nan Draoidhean's coined word into an Leabharlann's word-list in his own hand, under the day's entry, and never uses it again in anything he writes that year. The word stands unused on the page, unstruck and unbuilt upon.

events.title: Beathag marks the road's two names
events.body: Reading the new timetable at an Leabharlann, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh tells Sìleas nic Rath to mark the change beside the fuel's own spellings, saying a road keeps the name the men on it give it, not the name a board prints on a card.

events.title: Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean brought to an Leabharlann
events.body: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh brings the guild's rolls, its sick-roll and the oath-stone itself, worn smooth by two generations of thumbs, to an Leabharlann on a hired cart, and stands bare-headed in the rain through the whole of the unloading. Sìleas nic Rath, Beathag being away at Àth dhìreach, signs for the goods herself.

events.title: Tormod's letter copied into the record
events.body: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh gives Sìleas nic Rath a letter to be copied into an Leabharlann's record rather than filed among the guild's other papers, saying the guild had outlived the mountain's patience. Sìleas copies it that evening in a hand made to match Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's own.

events.title: The first Tuathach family bathed at Muileann ruadh
events.body: In an Lùnastal a woman of Doire ghlas, brought south by her married daughter for a chest complaint, bathes at the springs below Muileann ruadh, the first Tuathach the house has ever taken in. The keeper shows her to the basin as she would show anyone and asks no leave of the custodians.

events.title: Forty-one hands marked
events.body: By the time her slip-box is full Sìleas nic Rath has marked in forty-one of the sixty hands that write regularly to an Leabharlann the month each first wrote of the fuel without the man's name.

events.title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh stands bareheaded at the handing-over
events.body: The last master of Comann nan Gualadairean stands in the rain in the yard of an Leabharlann with his hat off through the whole unloading of the guild's goods, and asks no receipt but that it be said they came whole and not begged for.

events.title: The sick of the springs under Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail
events.body: When Comann nan Gualadairean' bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh of Muileann ruadh passes to Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, its custodians keep the old keeper on and take in the same sick, hewers' widows first, as the guild's rule had.

events.title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh returns to Seann Toll
events.body: In am Faoilleach, against a doctor's plain advice, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh travels once more to Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll to see how the removed families of Muileann dhearg fare in their first hard frost, though his chest has troubled him since the summer before.

events.title: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies at Seann Toll
events.body: Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies a little before dawn on the sixth of an Gearran, in a house of Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll, of a fever that settled on his chest. Gilleasbaig Ruadh sits with him through the two nights before the doctor can come, and the Row buries him themselves at the edge of the flood-plain.

events.title: Beathag enters Tormod's death herself
events.body: Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh's death into the day's page in her own hand, without asking her clerk to write it first, and sets beside the bare date his own line, that the guild had outlived the mountain's patience, and under it, smaller, that he had not.

events.title: The guild's oath above the pumps
events.body: The buyer of the old hall of Comann nan Gualadairean at Achadh dhomhain leaves the lintel with the guild's oath cut into it where it is, above the dubhan pumps, since cutting it out would bring the front of the house down.

events.title: Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the tip-heaps at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: Before selling his house's last share in An Sloc Mòr, Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the spoil-heaps above Achadh dhomhain with his clerk, ground his family has held a right to for four generations and never before had reason to stand on.

events.title: Comhairle nam Mèinnean buys An Sloc Mòr's last private share
events.body: Comhairle nam Mèinnean takes Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's remaining share in An Sloc Mòr's spoil and quarry-rights at a price haggled down only a little from the house's own asking, glad to hold the whole of An Sloc Mòr in its own hand at last.

events.title: The first Mac Ùisdein hull takes shape at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The first of three dubhan hulls bought with An Sloc Mòr's price is laid down at Ros dhomhain, a coastal trader with her tank amidships and her old grate left in for wood as well, should it ever come to that.

events.title: A bus line reaches Cathair mhòr
events.body: A second dubhan bus line opens between the capital and Cathair mhòr, Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's own town, carrying passengers the eleven miles in under an hour where the old coach took the better part of a morning.

events.title: The coal caste holds its tongue
events.body: The old coal-holding families of the capital say nothing that anyone writes down of the bus, the hired car or the trade turning wholly to dubhan; those with a seam still paying hold their peace because it pays, and those whose seams are spent do quietly, each in its own season, what Taigh Mhic Ùisdein has already done.

events.title: Bus and tacsaidh at the bridge
events.body: At the foot of the bridge in Cathair dhearg the dubhan buses load for Inis mhòr and Cathair mhòr and the hired cars wait for fares; the town calls them by the humans' names, bus and tacsaidh, and nobody coins others.

events.title: An Sloc Mòr's pumps run on dubhan
events.body: The engine-house at An Sloc Mòr changes its pumps from coal to dubhan, Comhairle nam Mèinnean finding it cheaper to buy the fuel than to burn its own coal.

events.title: A bus to the springs of Muileann ruadh
events.body: A bus of Cathair dhearg begins to run twice weekly to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh, and the custodians of the bath-house find their benches full of townsfolk who are not sick.

events.title: Peigi nic Ascaill reads Riaghailt na Cairte
events.body: Peigi nic Ascaill reads the grant chartering Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail and finds, near its foot, the clause fixing the guild's rolls to Dia-thìrich alone. She argues against the clause with Comann nan Sciobairean before the grant is confirmed, and is not heard.

events.title: Twelve masters sworn to Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail
events.body: Twelve masters, Peigi nic Ascaill among the first six called, swear Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' oath at the southern Seann Skell under a clerk of An t-Ionmhas and a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, while the Tuathaich fitters who trained beside them stand outside the roll being read.

events.title: Peigi nic Ascaill pays Joe Ashby a month over
events.body: The evening of the chartering, Peigi nic Ascaill brings Joe Ashby a month's wage over what is owed him and the two other Tuathaich fitters let go with him, and cannot bring herself to come further than his own doorstep to give it.

events.title: Joe Ashby fits Jean Fisher's boat
events.body: Back at Caol mhòr, Joe Ashby fits his first engine outside any guild, to the fishing boat of a widow named Jean Fisher, taking payment half in coin and half in fish.

events.title: The guild's letter pinned above Joe's bench
events.body: Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' court at Seann Skell writes north warning any who fit an engine without the guild's leave that they do so without its protection. Joe Ashby pins the letter above his bench at Caol mhòr rather than burn it.

events.title: Ruth Calder speaks and the five towns walk out
events.body: Ruth Calder, sent to Tional nan Tuathach that year in her dying father's stead, speaks for the western pit towns' right to cut their own coal as long as the seams allow, and leads the five towns' delegates out of the hall before the vote is entered in the book.

events.title: Martha Greaves keeps the granaries open to all five towns
events.body: Asked whether the walk-out closes Tional nan Tuathach's granaries to the western towns, Martha Greaves answers that a hungry household is a hungry household whatever its delegate voted, and the question is not put to her again that year.

events.title: The guild's banner blessed at Seann Skell
events.body: At the chartering of Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail in the works' long shed a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail blesses the guild's new banner, a black swan on grey, and twelve masters are sworn.

events.title: Abel Fowler mends a threshing engine at Muileann bheag
events.body: One of the fitters let go from the southern works under Riaghailt na Cairte is taken on at Muileann bheag, on the word of the lighthouse keeper, to mend a threshing engine none of the district's smiths will touch.

events.title: Cnoc bhàn's boats keep the pirate watch
events.body: In the year the raiders are taken off Ros dhomhain, the boats of Cnoc bhàn keep watch in turns on the pirate waters and twice put out to warn the fishing fleet in from the north-east.

events.title: The depots marked on an Leabharlann's map
events.body: Raghnall mac Mhuirich asks that the three new depots be marked on the front room's map, close together on the coast, and tells Sìleas nic Rath he expects the map will want marking again before the year is out, though he cannot say why he thinks it.

events.title: An t-Ionmhas's clerk's private letter
events.body: A clerk of An t-Ionmhas who owes Raghnall mac Mhuirich a kindness sends an Leabharlann a private account of the council's sitting of 5 an Cèitean ahead of the formal minute, noting that the two resolutions passed by a show of hands with no count taken, against the council's custom in so weighty a matter.

events.title: The torn proclamation from the market post
events.body: A carrier tears the printed proclamation from a post at Cathair dhearg and brings it up to an Leabharlann folded inside his own almanac, thinking Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh should see the notice as the market crowd had seen it, creased and a little torn at one corner.

events.title: Beathag begins the re-heading
events.body: The evening the proclamation reaches her, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh sits alone at the long table with her fourteen ledgers and begins to set the new heading, Linn an Dubhain and its year, beside the old heading of each, in a smaller hand, with a line drawn between them, leaving the old headings standing.

events.title: Beathag writes the line about moving a year
events.body: Finishing the re-heading before dawn, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes at the foot of the fifteenth year's page, in a smaller hand than her working hand, that never before has she had to move a year she was living in, and lets it stand uncorrected in the fair copy sent up to the council.

events.title: Gille-Easbaig Bàn's letter on the new dies
events.body: Gille-Easbaig Bàn writes to an Leabharlann that the mint has cut a plain seal for the coinage, the coal ink pressed into no die of it, and owns he does not know whether he is glad or sorry to be done with grinding an ink that had cost, that spring, more than the seal's own worth in coin.

events.title: The dies set beside the oath-stone
events.body: Raghnall mac Mhuirich sets Fearchar Bonn's worn dies in the glass case beside Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean, and remarks to Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh that everything lately brought into the case has just stopped being used.

events.title: Raghnall's three dots on an Leabharlann's map
events.body: The keeper of an Leabharlann has the chronicler's clerk mark the three new dubhan depots of the north on the old map in the front room, three dots close together on the coast.

events.title: The proclamation read at the Cuan shean harbour
events.body: At the harbour of Cuan shean the maor's crier reads the proclamation of Linn an Dubhain from the harbour steps to the fishing crews, who ask whether it changes the day of the fish-market. It does not.

events.title: A pump on the quays of Baile ghorm
events.body: The third anchorage of the kingdom, at Baile ghorm, sets a dubhan pump on its wolf-post quays for the fishing boats that have taken engines, the first on that coast.

events.title: Doire shean hears the new count at market
events.body: At Doire shean the new count of the years is read out at the Tuesday market; the market-clerk writes the next week's date both ways in his book and goes on doing so for a year.
